blindSummary: 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents were recorded in this state/province in 2025 — from a population of only ~1.4m, the highest per-capita incident load in the country. Counterweight: in July 2026 a county court found an attacker violated the state/province's civil-rights act after striking a trans gas-station employee, using his pronoun refusal as bias evidence, with bodycam showing officers correcting his pronoun use.
blindSourceSummaries: An LGBTQ media-monitoring group's release (January 2025): 1,042 anti-LGBTQ incidents tracked in 2025 across 47 states/provinces and the national capital district — 128 vandalism, 76 violent assaults, 22 mass-violence threats, 15 arson attempts; 51% of incidents targeted transgender and gender-nonconforming people, up 10% on 2024. Per-state tallies give this state/province 72 recorded incidents — an unusually large share of the national total for a population of ~1.4m, i.e. the highest per-capita load.

The state/province's public-radio and flagship newspaper (July 2026): a county superior court found a man who physically and verbally assaulted a transgender woman at her workplace in May 2024 violated the state/province's civil-rights act — ordering three years' no contact (350 ft from her, her home and workplace) and a $5,000 fine, alongside a separate guilty plea to second-degree assault with a suspended sentence; the prosecuting authority treated his refusal to use her pronouns, captured on bodycam during questioning, as evidence of bias motive.
blindTangential: Anti-trans campaigners took legal action against a small school district over a trans athlete — local climate pressure rather than a state/province-wide rule, but part of the same visibility conflict.
